column8: At 14 weeks with strong food aversions; her husband cooks every meal.
column9: My husband has been amazing and has been cooking every single meal. I feel bad that he’s probably getting whiplash, but he’s also incredibly understanding.

column8: What a pregnant friend does about deli meat on her OB's suggestion.
column9: She said she’s just been boiling or frying all the deli meat she eats (at the suggestion of her OB), and of course, that makes me feel too disgusted to eat it!

column8: Two weeks after the birth, posting that a fear she read about online did not come true.
column9: I love my dog so much still, and even more so watching him gently sniff at my new little baby and knowing they’re going to be best friends so soon.

column8: Why she posted.
column9: while I was pregnant, I was afraid I’d get home and automatically hate my dog. Just wanted to post here that this is not the case for everyone. Because it was a genuine fear of mine during pregnancy.

column8: Seven weeks after the birth, selling their home; family stays one after another.
column9: My mother in law stayed with us for two months so she could be there when he was born and stay a while after. As soon as she left my brother moved in with his dog so we can help him through the beginning of a divorce/separation.

column8: How they cut costs.
column9: I’m not working, we’ve been cloth diapering to save money and I’m washing them almost every night.

column8: Her husband helps but works.
column9: I have help from him, but he works while I’m at home so I do have to take on the majority of baby and house work.

column8: Why she saves the disposable nappies from her shower.
column9: Financially, disposable diapers aren’t really an option. We do have disposables from our baby shower to fall back on when I need to.

column8: After commenters' suggestions.
column9: I definitely need to apply for WIC. I don’t mind cleaning the diapers so much, I just mind when I have to clean the diapers, cook dinner, put it away and do the dishes all in the same day.

column8: First pregnancy after years of trying; every risk feels bigger.
column9: recently pregnant for first time after many years of trying and failing. So it feels a bit like "this is my one shot"

column8: Her doctor's response when she asked about testing.
column9: I did ask my doc about getting tested and they shrugged off my concerns.

column8: First-time mother at 19 weeks overheard a new doctor about her weight.
column9: I could hear her talking about me outside the office door “did she really gain this much weight this month?” and knew I was in for an interesting appointment.

column8: What the new doctor did at the appointment.
column9: She came in to see me and told me she was putting me on the gestational diabetes diet and lectured me about needing to exercise. I walk 2-3 miles daily already.

column8: Her mother's reaction.
column9: My mom was LIVID to say the least and told me it’s ridiculous I’ve been put on the GD diet before even taking the test and that no one had ever spoken to her that way during her 3 pregnancies.

column8: Worried this doctor may deliver her baby.
column9: yeah her delivering is what I’m worried about now honestly. I know i can’t fully control it and again I recognize what she was sharing with me is hard.. it’s just the way she delivered it. The bedside manner was just not there

column8: Pregnant with an 11-month-old who is into everything; her husband works a lot.
column9: I’m soo damn exhausted, my husband works a lot so I do most of everything.

column8: After a hard bedtime.
column9: like it’s really putting me off have another baby, like I’m currently sitting crying my eyes out because I’m getting so overwhelmed, when does this stop? Will he ever calm down

column8: Her sister, 12 weeks pregnant and alone, lives on a small fixed income.
column9: Her monthly fixed income is around $1,600, and 950 of that goes to rent alone. She usually has 100 - 200 dollars left after paying bills.

column8: Living abroad, she doesn't know where to start finding help for her sister.
column9: I have no idea how to even go about finding government support, or maybe a social worker or something that could help her out in the coming months.

column8: Her plan to fly in around the birth.
column9: I plan on going back there for a couple months around the time she will be giving birth so that she has an extra hand leading up to it, and someone to help her get through the first weeks which I hear are really tough.

column8: First-time mother at 39 weeks after several triage visits with negative tests.
column9: My husband keeps saying I’m crazy and it’s super frustrating and embarrassing getting in the car after being in OB triage.

column8: About the hospital's nurses.
column9: Also the hospital has a very rude ob nurse staff and they haven’t helped either.

column8: At 22 weeks, anger and grief about her relationship with her mother.
column9: She can be loving but also guilt-tripping, emotionally unpredictable, and dismissive of boundaries.

column8: Entering week 10, sick all day; making a bingo game for friends and family.
column9: It should honestly just be called "The sickness" because of course its not just in the mornings.

column8: Her way of coping.
column9: Today after finding myself puking in a Costco trashcan I decided the only way I could truly deal with this ordeal is through humor, so I've decided to make a bingo game to give to my friends and family.

column8: Just found out she is pregnant; a work trip to Milan falls at 6-7 weeks.
column9: the work part after the start of 7 weeks is gonna be pretty hands on and I’ll need to use my brain- so that coupled with being in a foreign country is kinda terrifying. afraid of having to leave mid meeting to go throw up, etc. lol.

column8: First-time mother at 40+3.
column9: I feel like it’s the curse of social media, where I rarely see people making it to their due date and going at 36-39 weeks so now I feel down about the fact I didn’t do that.

column8: What people around her keep asking.
column9: Also doesn’t help when everyone around me keeps asking “when” like I can predict when baby will make his grand entrance.

column8: What her midwife told her.
column9: My midwife told me most ftm’s go to 41 weeks and 2 days as an average statistic but that sounds miserable.

column8: First-time mother at 13 weeks upset by her body and by weight posts in pregnancy groups.
column9: Or people posting and seemingly bragging in pregnancy groups about how they’ve “only gained (XYZ) pounds “ in their whole pregnancy. Please save it.

column8: What she sees on social media.
column9: It doesn’t help that we currently live in a world obsessed with GLP1s, and every time I open social media I see a pregnant person who is stick thin aside from their belly
